issues.body:
At exec.rs:4643-4652 the label is built as `BGP [{plan}] (...)` where `plan` is `"binary GOO"` or `"worst-case-optimal (LFTJ)"`, and the new suffix is appended under only `patterns.len() >= 3 && crate::dp::active().is_some()` — the `bgp_uses_binary` discriminant is ignored.

But `eval_bgp` routes `patterns.len() >= 3 && bgp_is_cyclic(patterns)` to `eval_bgp_wcoj` (exec.rs:6722) BEFORE `eval_bgp_binary`, and the DP hook (`if let Some(cfg) = crate::dp::active() { eval_bgp_dp(..) }`) exists only inside `eval_bgp_binary` (exec.rs:6952). `bgp_uses_binary` is exactly `!(len >= 3 && bgp_is_cyclic(..))` (exec.rs:6893), so `plan == "worst-case-optimal (LFTJ)"` implies `len >= 3` and implies DPccp is unreachable for that BGP.

Consequence: every cyclic 3+-pattern BGP now renders as `BGP [worst-case-optimal (LFTJ)] (n patterns, m filters) [DPccp may execute; displayed tree is a greedy replay, not an execution record]`. Both halves of that suffix are false for this node — DPccp cannot execute it, and an LFTJ node is not a greedy replay (it has no greedy join order at all; the WCOJ renderer prints a global variable order, not a join sequence).

This leaks into the structured `explain-json` `operator` field too, since `trace_label_pub` (exec.rs:4633) forwards to `trace_label` — so the sq-jbqh4 JSON plan tree carries the false planner annotation on cyclic nodes.

It is also internally inconsistent: `explain.rs` places the equivalent NOTE only after the `!exec::bgp_uses_binary(&patterns)` early return (explain.rs:289-313, note at 324-331), i.e. correctly scoped to the binary branch. The two explain surfaces now disagree on the same query, and skills/http-server/SKILL.md's claim that EXPLAIN labels "a DP-eligible BGP" as a greedy replay does not hold for the ineligible cyclic case.
issues.fix_hint: Gate the suffix on the already-computed binary/LFTJ discriminant so it mirrors explain.rs, e.g. compute `let binary = bgp_uses_binary(&patterns);` once, use it for `plan`, and require it in the disclosure condition: `if binary && patterns.len() >= 3 && crate::dp::active().is_some()`. Then add a regression test alongside the two new ones in crates/sparq-server/tests/explain_metrics.rs (or an engine-level test) that pins the NEGATIVE case: a cyclic 3-pattern BGP (e.g. `?a ex:p ?b . ?b ex:q ?c . ?c ex:r ?a`) must render `worst-case-optimal` WITHOUT the DPccp suffix in both the text ANALYZE trace and the explain-json operator label. Without a negative-case test the disclosure predicate stays unpinned in either direction.
issues.title: trace_label attaches the DPccp disclosure to worst-case-optimal (LFTJ) BGPs, where DPccp provably cannot execute

issues.body:
The header says "This file is gated on the server feature so deliberate lean builds remain valid", but the actual gate is `#![cfg(feature = "dp-planner")]` (line 9). The rest of the paragraph ("Removing `dp-planner` from `default` therefore silently skips it") only makes sense for a `dp-planner` gate, so this is a stale/incorrect sentence rather than a design statement. The precedent file crates/sparq-server/tests/algebra_rewrite_default.rs:6 names its gate correctly ("Gated on this crate's own `algebra-rewrite` feature"), so the drift is local to this new file.

Separately, the file is honest that it is not a default-set-membership witness, which is good — but that means nothing in this PR fails if `dp-planner` is later dropped from `default`, even though "the shipped binary matches the CLI" is the stated goal of the change.
issues.fix_hint: Reword line 5 to "This file is gated on this crate's own `dp-planner` feature" (matching algebra_rewrite_default.rs:6). If a real default-membership tripwire is wanted, consider a `#[cfg(all(feature = "default", not(feature = "dp-planner")))] compile_error!(..)`-style guard or a CI assertion over `cargo metadata` on sparq-server's default feature list, rather than relying on a test that compiles out exactly when the invariant breaks.
issues.title: Module doc states the file is gated on the `server` feature; it is gated on `dp-planner`

issues.body:
The Cargo comment and SKILL say planning "is bounded but does not poll QueryBudget cancellation". That is accurate, but the reachable bound is worth stating concretely because dense join graphs are NOT excluded by the cyclic->LFTJ routing: `bgp_is_cyclic` is a hypergraph (GYO) test, so a star BGP where n patterns all share one variable is ACYCLIC and takes the binary path, yet its pattern-adjacency graph is a CLIQUE. A ~12-pattern star (`SELECT * WHERE { ?x :p1 ?a . ?x :p2 ?b . ... }`, trivially small to send) yields 4095 connected subgraphs — just under `DEFAULT_MAX_SUBGRAPHS = 4096` (dp.rs:65) — so it passes the csg guard and proceeds to enumerate ~261k csg/cmp pairs into a `Vec<(u64,u64)>` (~4 MB) plus a sort and an FxHashMap DP table, per such BGP, per in-flight request, entirely between coarse budget check sites (exec.rs:61-62 documents the budget as "checked at COARSE sites only"). Multiple such BGPs per query (UNION branches / subqueries) multiply the transient allocation.

This is bounded and the `query_timeout` + TIMEOUT_GRACE 503 path (http.rs:224-228) still guarantees a response, so it is not a blocker — but it is a new memory/CPU amplification factor introduced by default on a network-facing binary, and the current docs describe only the CPU aspect.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) have the server install a conservative planner budget for request-path queries via `sparq_engine::with_dp_planner_budget(<smaller cap>, ..)` so the server does not inherit the CLI's 4096 default, or (b) extend the Cargo.toml/SKILL note with the concrete worst case (up to `max_subgraphs * PAIR_BUDGET_FACTOR` = 524288 emitted pairs, several MB transient, per BGP, not budget-polled) and explicitly mention that star-shaped BGPs are acyclic yet produce clique join graphs — so an operator can size the risk instead of inferring that only "large/dense" queries are affected.
issues.title: Default-on DPccp adds an uncancellable per-BGP planning cost to the unauthenticated HTTP surface; the documented bound understates the reachable worst case

issues.body: The opt-out instruction is correct for a per-crate build (`cargo build -p sparq-server --no-default-features --features server,jsonld`), but sparq-cli (Cargo.toml:146) and sparq-py (Cargo.toml:58) enable `dp-planner`/`algebra-rewrite`/`antijoin-static-decline` unconditionally on their `sparq-engine` dependency, so a whole-workspace build re-lights the engine features regardless of sparq-server's own feature set. crates/sparq-server/tests/dp_planner_default.rs already records this caveat ("A whole-workspace build may also unify the engine feature through another crate"), and algebra_rewrite_default.rs:17-20 records it too, but the user-facing README and SKILL blockquote do not — an operator following the hardening advice from the docs alone could believe they have a planner-dark binary when they do not.
issues.fix_hint: Add a half-sentence to the README bullet and the SKILL blockquote: the opt-out is authoritative for a per-crate build (`-p sparq-server`); a `--workspace` build can unify `sparq-engine/dp-planner` in via sparq-cli/sparq-py. Verify the shipped artifact with the per-crate build command.
issues.title: "Drop them via --no-default-features --features server,jsonld" omits the workspace feature-unification caveat

verdict.summary:
The core idea (EXPLAIN must disclose that the displayed tree is a greedy replay when DPccp may actually execute the BGP) is sound, and most of it is implemented correctly: the `patterns.len() >= 3` threshold matches `dp::plan`'s real floor (`!(3..=MAX_PATTERNS).contains(&n) -> None`, dp.rs:507), `dp::active()` is the right liveness probe, the feature forwarding compiles (sparq-core/sparq-engine are non-optional deps of sparq-server), the parity claim is true (sparq-cli/Cargo.toml:146 enables dp-planner+algebra-rewrite+antijoin-static-decline on its engine dep), and the new tests are non-vacuous (the 3-pattern star BGP is hypergraph-acyclic, connected, and within budget, so DPccp genuinely plans it).

One major defect blocks approval: in `exec.rs::trace_label` the disclosure is appended without checking `bgp_uses_binary`, so it is also attached to `BGP [worst-case-optimal (LFTJ)]` labels. `eval_bgp` routes `patterns.len() >= 3 && bgp_is_cyclic(..)` to `eval_bgp_wcoj` (exec.rs:6722), and the DP hook lives only inside `eval_bgp_binary` (exec.rs:6952) — DPccp provably cannot execute a cyclic BGP. Every cyclic 3+-pattern BGP therefore gets a false annotation in both the ANALYZE text trace and the structured explain-json `operator` field (via `trace_label_pub`), telling the user the LFTJ tree "is not an execution record" when it is exactly that. `explain.rs` gets this right (the note sits after the `!bgp_uses_binary` early return at line 313), so the two explain surfaces now disagree, and the SKILL text ("EXPLAIN labels a DP-eligible BGP as a greedy replay") is contradicted for the ineligible cyclic case. Since the whole purpose of this PR is EXPLAIN honesty, an over-disclosure that misdescribes a real execution path is a substantive correctness issue, not cosmetic.

Remaining items are minor: a module-doc mismatch in the new server test, an under-documented planner-cost surface, and a docs caveat about workspace feature unification.
